title: Audio capture: microphone on both systems, call audio on Windows, Mac microphone permission check
story: Grillo can now record the room microphone on Windows and Mac, and the call audio on Windows, sending the sound to the main process as 5-second slices in the format the speech model reads. Before recording it checks the microphone permission, and the member can pick which microphone to use. Nothing appears on screen yet: the meeting screen's record button comes with its own story. Nothing earlier was replaced.

checks.criterion: startCapture({ source: microphone }) sends 5-second 16 kHz mono slices to main, and stopCapture() ends the capture
checks.steps: Start Grillo on Windows or Mac with a microphone plugged in. Start a microphone recording. Speak for 15 seconds. Stop.
checks.expected: About three slices arrive in main, the last one shorter. No error is shown.

checks.criterion: On Windows, call audio records what the speakers play
checks.steps: Start Grillo on Windows. Play any sound, such as a test video. Start a call-audio recording for 15 seconds. Stop.
checks.expected: No picker or permission prompt appears, and about three slices arrive carrying the sound.

checks.criterion: On a Mac, choosing call audio gives a typed unsupported result
checks.steps: Start Grillo on a Mac. Choose call-audio recording.
checks.expected: A message says Mac call audio is not available yet and suggests the room microphone. Nothing is recorded.

checks.criterion: A refused microphone is reported with where to grant it
checks.steps: Turn Grillo off under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone (Mac), or turn off Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone > Let desktop apps access your microphone (Windows). Start a microphone recording.
checks.expected: No recording starts, and that system's exact instruction is shown.

checks.criterion: The member can list the microphones and pick one
checks.steps: Plug in a second microphone. Open the microphone list and pick the second one. Record. Unplug it and record again.
checks.expected: The list shows both microphones. The first recording uses the picked one. The second says the picked microphone is not connected and does not switch to another.
